clue.text: Plan by sheep to wander round

indicators.note: round says the wandering word goes around the sheep word

parts.note: to wander or roam is to stray
a teg is a sheep in its second year

explanation.surface: A scheme hatched by a sheep to roam about the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy is an overall plan of action, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Something a bit fishy's raised with endless subtlety and disdain

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: fins are a bit of a fish, so something fishy; the 's adds the S

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off the word for subtlety

parts.note: finesse is subtlety or delicate skill

explanation.surface: A suspicious smell is detected alongside subtle disdain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns FINS into SNIF; 'endless' drops the final E of FINESSE, leaving FINESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sniffiness is a haughty, contemptuous attitude, a synonym of disdain.

clue.text: Pal rode off, embarrassed after climbing this?

definitions.text: Pal rode off, embarrassed after climbing this?

indicators.note: after says the second piece comes later in the answer
off says the letters of these words are set off in a new order
in a down clue, climbing means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red

explanation.surface: A friend fled in embarrassment after scaling something, perhaps a lover's escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges PAL RODE into ROPELAD; 'climbing' turns RED into DER. The whole clue also pictures someone fleeing down from a balcony.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes a getaway: a flexible ladder is what an embarrassed lover might have climbed and then fled down.

clue.text: A time wine goes with duck

parts.note: tent is a deep red Spanish wine
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: A drinker mixes wine with a duck dish.
explanation.walkthrough: TENT is an old name for a dark red Spanish wine used for communion; duck is O, a zero score in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Ten to is a time on the clock, as in ten minutes before the hour.

clue.text: Become anxious and burp?

definitions.meaning: to become alarmed or nervous, a British idiom
read literally, bringing up gas from the stomach

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to become nervous, and literally it describes bringing up wind as a burp does.

clue.text: Ground-breaking quarterdeck?

definitions.meaning: digging tools that break the ground
one of the four suits, so a quarter of a pack of cards

explanation.definitionFit: Spades are digging tools, and spades is also one of the four suits that make up a deck of cards.

clue.text: Novelist in setter's company at the races

parts.note: Puck, the setter, was Paul Facey-Hunter, so the setter's is Paul's
the TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle races

explanation.surface: A writer joins the puzzle-setter's party at a race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter Puck's real first name was Paul. The TT are motorcycle races held on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Scott was the English novelist who wrote The Raj Quartet, so he is an example of a novelist.

clue.text: See 8
Tout had short new catch phrase

indicators.note: new says these letters are made into something new, a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A ticket tout came up short of a new slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges TOUT HAD SHORT. The phrase was the catchphrase of Larry Grayson, a camp British TV comedian and game-show host.
explanation.definitionFit: This line was the famous catchphrase of comedian Larry Grayson, so it is an example of a catchphrase.

clue.text: No recriminations with this setter's wordplay? Shame, given the execution

parts.note: this setter's is read as 'this setter is', which the setter says as I'm
a pun is a piece of wordplay

indicators.note: being executed, beheaded, means losing the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a shame, as in 'what a pity', is a pity

explanation.surface: A setter claims a pun shouldn't be punished, though it is a shame it got executed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given the execution' beheads PITY, leaving ITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Impunity is exemption from punishment or harmful consequences, so no recriminations follow.

clue.text: Sound work-out regularly provided by this puzzle

indicators.note: regularly says every other letter is taken, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A good mental workout comes from doing this puzzle often.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudoku is a number-placement puzzle, so it is an example of a puzzle.

clue.text: Ground near Selby that's out of fashion? Kiss performed there often

indicators.note: out of says the rearranged letters lie outside the word for fashion
ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are pounded into a new order

parts.note: ton is fashion or style, as in 'the ton' of society

explanation.surface: A Yorkshire ground near Selby has gone out of fashion, though people often kiss there.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram gives BLARNEYSE, which 'out of' wraps around the fashion word. Selby is a Yorkshire town; the stone is at Blarney Castle in Ireland, kissed for eloquence.
explanation.definitionFit: Visitors kiss the stone at Blarney Castle to gain the gift of the gab, so this is where a kiss is often performed.

clue.text: A bad argument is like a riddle!

definitions.meaning: a weak argument is said to have many flaws
a riddle is a coarse sieve, which is perforated all over

explanation.definitionFit: A flawed argument is full of gaps, and a riddle, a sieve, is literally pierced with gaps.

clue.text: Drug brought 'rush' for each self-indulgent person

parts.note: E is ecstasy, the drug
got, as in got something home, means brought
rip means to rush along, as in rip down the road
per means for each

explanation.surface: A drug delivered a rush for each person who indulges.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego-tripper is someone acting to satisfy their own vanity, a self-indulgent person.

clue.text: Doctor's eight points under 'The ability to wear well'

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
eight compass points: E, S, S, S, E, N, S, E

explanation.surface: A doctor's notes score eight points under a heading about clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' is a link here: the doctor and points are filed under the definition. Compass points E, S and N are standard crossword letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dress sense is skill at choosing clothes that suit one, the ability to wear things well.

clue.text: Knobs turned Sun editor on

indicators.note: turned says the run of pieces is read back to front

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sunday or sun

explanation.surface: A tabloid editor is turned on by knobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodes are knobs or knots, small lumps or swellings.

clue.text: Divert river through CID stake-out

indicators.note: through says the river letter runs right through the other letters
out says the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: Detectives on a stake-out are diverted by a river through the area.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram gives SIDETACK, and 'through' puts the river letter inside. CID is the British police's Criminal Investigation Department, whose detectives mount stake-outs.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidetrack is to divert someone from their main purpose, a synonym.

clue.text: Half of America's wrong about Bush, allegedly

indicators.note: about says the letters are moved about into a new order
half of says only the first half of the word is used

explanation.surface: Half of America thinks it was wrong about President Bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' takes AMER from AMERICA, and 'about' rearranges AMER with WRONG.
explanation.definitionFit: George W Bush's critics called him a warmonger for the Iraq war, so allegedly he is one.

clue.text: Speed can't upset one's footwork?

indicators.note: upset says the letters are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A dancer cannot keep up speed, upsetting their footwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Step dance is dancing whose essence is intricate foot movements, an example of footwork.

clue.text: Boob by the Guardian brings letter from Paul

parts.note: tit is slang for a boob or a foolish person, also a breast
the Guardian newspaper speaking of itself is us

explanation.surface: A newspaper blunder prompts a letter from one of its setters.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul is the Guardian setter but here the Apostle: the Epistle to Titus is one of St Paul's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Epistle to Titus is a New Testament letter attributed to St Paul.

clue.text: No pork pies? Model regrets having the blues

parts.note: the Model T was the famous Ford car
to rue is to regret
the Tories, Britain's Conservatives, have blue as their colour

explanation.surface: A model with no pies regrets feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pork pies' is Cockney rhyming slang for lies, so no pork pies are true accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Pork pies means lies in rhyming slang, so their opposite is true stories, accounts that really happened.

clue.text: Reared some geese, bought to get fat

indicators.note: Reared says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A farmer raised some geese, bought to be fattened.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'to get fat' is a verb phrase; the answer is an adjective, so 'fat' alone defines it and 'to get' is a link. In a down clue 'Reared' reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means extremely overweight, so it is a stronger synonym of fat.

clue.text: See 8
Fixture in four-sided 'round' house

definitions.meaning: a match in the round contested by the last four teams
a house joined to one neighbour on one side

explanation.definitionFit: A semi is short both for a semi-final, the round of four, and for a semi-detached house.

clue.text: Heard male prostitute talk out of his ass?

indicators.note: heard says the words are spoken, and the answer sounds like them

parts.note: a he-whore is jokingly a male prostitute

explanation.surface: Someone reportedly heard a gigolo talking nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken in an accent, he-whore sounds like the bray. 'talk out of his ass' is literal: the sound a donkey makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Hee-haw is the braying noise a donkey makes, its literal talk.

clue.text: Simple menu Posh arranged

indicators.note: arranged says the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A plain menu laid out by a posh person or a Spice Girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Homespun means plain and unsophisticated, a synonym of simple.

clue.text: Awkward tart's customer needing 'a little yogurt'

parts.note: a trick is slang for a prostitute's client

indicators.note: a little says just a small part, the first letter, of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A tart's customer awkwardly needs a pot of yogurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tart' looks like a pastry beside the yogurt, but means a prostitute.
explanation.definitionFit: Tricky means difficult or awkward to deal with, a synonym.

clue.text: Once more try getting on Home Counties train

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again, once more
to hear a case is to try it in court
the Home Counties around London are in the South East, SE

explanation.surface: Someone tries again to board a Home Counties train.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in England's South East.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to practise or drill, so to train for a performance.
